items.passage:
A nursery logbook records four seed lots given the same coating.
One: a fescue lot at Hollin Bank, coated 4 March, showed germination 9 points above the previous spring sowing when scored 26 March; logged by Marek.
Two: a fescue lot at Hollin Bank, coated 5 March, showed germination 6 points above the previous spring sowing when scored 27 March; logged by Marek.
House air temperature matched the earlier sowing to a tenth of a degree, and every lot sat on an open bench, taking the house air directly. Rates cover every tray sown from each lot, full coat or partial, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed.
Three: a fescue lot at Hollin Bank, coated 6 March, showed germination 11 points above the previous spring sowing when scored 28 March; logged by Marek.
Four: a fescue lot at Hollin Bank, coated 7 March, showed germination 7 points above the previous spring sowing when scored 29 March; logged by Marek.
Each figure was copied into the nursery ledger and initialled by the head grower.
items.notes: Check that all four cases carry one distinct value per dimension (Hollin Bank, fescue, spring, Marek) and that only the coating dates, point gains and scoring dates vary. The closer holds the obvious rivals for a season-over-season comparison fixed - bench temperature, watering schedule, seed batch, growing medium - which is what makes the self-comparison adequate. Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_false.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the rates over the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and the clause beside it records that about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed. The claim is about the germination of the coated lot, so the population is every tray sown from it and the germination points describe four fifths of that. Seed that takes a full coat is the plump, well-filled grain, while the light and cracked seed comes off the coater thinly covered, so a rate built on the fully coated trays alone sits above the lot's own rate, and the 9, 6, 11 and 7 point gains are consistent with each lot's germination being unchanged. All four lots are fescue at Hollin Bank in one spring under grower Marek, so the same missing fifth sits under every case.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Confirm the closer names exactly one alternative cause (a warmer bench) and that it works only because the four lots are coherent - one nursery, one season, one bench. Check the vocabulary against the TRUE closer: both talk about watering schedule, seed batch, growing medium and bench temperature, so the difference is logical (matched vs four degrees above), not lexical.
